name: Evolution of Life
description: Life on Earth from the first cells to the dinosaurs, the age of mammals, the first humans and the animals people drove to extinction, and how Darwin explained it.

checkpoints.name: The early Earth
checkpoints.note: The young Earth is struck by a planet the size of Mars, and the debris forms the Moon. The surface is molten at first, then cools, and oceans form.

checkpoints.name: First life
checkpoints.note: Single cells appear in the sea. Some learn to use sunlight and fill the air with oxygen, the planet freezes over at least twice, and the first large animals appear.

checkpoints.name: Life fills the seas and the land
checkpoints.note: In the Cambrian explosion most animal groups appear. Fish grow jaws, plants and insects move onto land, forests spread and amphibians and reptiles follow. The worst extinction of all ends the age.

checkpoints.name: The age of dinosaurs
checkpoints.note: Dinosaurs rise in the Triassic and rule the land for 165 million years, from Brachiosaurus to Tyrannosaurus. Birds, mammals and flowers appear, and an asteroid ends it all.

checkpoints.name: The age of mammals
checkpoints.note: With the dinosaurs gone, mammals grow large and spread across every continent and into the sea. Grasslands spread, the Himalayas rise and apes appear in Africa.

checkpoints.name: The first humans
checkpoints.note: Apes in Africa start to walk upright. Australopithecus makes the first stone tools, and Homo erectus tames fire and walks out of Africa.

checkpoints.name: Homo sapiens
checkpoints.note: Our species appears in Africa and spreads around the world, meeting Neanderthals on the way. As people arrive, mammoths, giant birds and later the dodo disappear.

checkpoints.name: Darwin and today
checkpoints.note: Darwin and Wallace explain evolution by natural selection, and Mendel finds the laws of heredity. People drive more species to extinction while science learns to read and edit the code of life.
